statement: In the same 7 adults with recreational MDMA experience (one double-blind, placebo-controlled sleep-laboratory study), the evidence is insufficient to say whether a single laboratory dose of MDMA makes people sleepier the next day. On next-day nap tests, sleepiness after the MDMA night did not differ significantly from the placebo night, but it did not differ from a night of shortened sleep either, which clearly made people sleepier than placebo, according to the Results text (the paper's figure legend instead reports the shortened night as different from both, and in the figure MDMA sits close to placebo); on the day after the recovery night, the three conditions did not differ. The values for each condition are shown only in a figure, 7 people are too few to rule out a real difference, and the study measured no next-day mood, thinking or tiredness ratings. The authors' conclusion that MDMA's sleep loss did not produce daytime sleepiness rests on this non-difference. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: The day after a night in a sleep lab, people's sleepiness was measured with short nap tests. After a short night of sleep without MDMA they fell asleep much faster than after a dummy pill. After MDMA they were somewhere in between and not clearly different from either, so this small study cannot say whether MDMA makes you sleepier the next day. Mood and thinking were not measured.
population: Adults aged 19 to 34 (5 men, 2 women) with at least three recent recreational MDMA uses (lifetime mean 27), screened free of psychiatric disorders and drug or alcohol dependence
exposure: A single oral dose of pure MDMA given by the researchers before a night in the sleep laboratory (amount and timing are study conditions in the study card)
comparator: The same people's day after a placebo night and day after a placebo night with shortened time in bed
outcome: Next-day objective sleepiness (multiple sleep latency test: mean sleep latency and sleep-onset REM periods)
magnitude: Treatment by day interaction F(2,12) = 4.63, P = 0.032; post hoc, shortened sleep gave a shorter mean sleep latency than placebo (falling to about 6 minutes), while MDMA differed from neither placebo nor shortened sleep (condition means only in a figure); sleep-onset REM periods 1.43 after MDMA, 1.00 after placebo and 2.14 after shortened sleep, not significantly different.

evidence.extracted: Treatment by day interaction F = 4.63 (df 2 and 12), P = 0.032; after shortened sleep the mean nap-test latency was shorter than after placebo (about 6 minutes, per the Discussion), while after MDMA it differed neither from placebo nor from shortened sleep, per the Results text; the Figure 4 legend instead reports shortened sleep as shorter than both placebo and MDMA (P = 0.031), and in the figure the MDMA bar is close to placebo; no differences on the day after the recovery night; sleep-onset REM periods 2.14 (shortened sleep), 1.43 (MDMA), 1.00 (placebo), not significant.

evidence.locator: Abstract › Measurements and Results and Conclusions; Discussion, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Results › Effects on the MSLT, 1st paragraph; Figure 4 legend
evidence.extracted: The authors conclude that MDMA's sleep loss was not associated with next-day sleepiness and that next-day sleep latency remained at placebo levels; with 7 participants, MDMA's next-day values were not significantly different from those after shortened sleep either, per the Results text (the Figure 4 legend reports the opposite).

risk_of_bias.note: Incomplete Latin square; two withdrawals; objective nap tests.

indirectness.note: Worded for one laboratory dose with a full night in bed.

imprecision.note: Seven people; no values or intervals for the MDMA condition.

grade.reasoning: A placebo-controlled within-person laboratory study with counterbalanced order starts high. Risk of bias -1 (incomplete counterbalancing, two withdrawals). Imprecision -2 (7 people; the MDMA condition differed from neither comparison; values only in a figure). Very low. 'Insufficient evidence' because neither an effect nor its absence can be shown.
